mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a decline in demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of reduced economic activity and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST decreases by more than 5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month suggests a surge in supply-side activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both PAYEMS and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the periods where RSAFS increases consistently over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it suggests inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates remain low.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: low interest rate environment with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL meet the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with a rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5%, indicates supply-side constraints and inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as input costs rise and output falls.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where both INDPRO and CPIAUCSL meet the trigger conditions.
